To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the yields of complex-fragment emission are in conformity with statistical model predictions, and the time scales of various fragment emissions are in conformity with predictions of the dynamical model of deep inelastic collisions.

the fully energy-dampened fragment yields are in conformity with statistical model predictions; the angular distributions of the fully energy- dampened fragment emission are isotropic; the angular momentum dissipation is close to the corresponding value of the sticking limit.

(1) the yields of complex fragments from fully energy-damped reactions are in conformity to the statistical model predictions, (2) the time scales of the fragment emissions in the deep inelastic reactions are comparable to those in the fusion-fission reactions, and (3) the angular momentum dissipation is close to the respective sticking limit value
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of fusion-fission and deep inelastic processes in low energy heavy ion collisions.
the study of the emission of complex fragments in low-energy light-ions collisions.
the complex-fragment production in light-ion induced reactions and its dependence on the reaction partners and the excitation energy of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deep inelastic fragment emission process is a very fast and highly damped process, and the angular momentum dissipation is close to the sticking limit.

the complex-fragment emissions in low-energy light-heavy-ion reactions are governed by the statistical model for the fully energy-dammed fragments while the deep inelastic fragment emission is governed by the sticking limit for the angular momentum dissipation.
the complex-fragment emission in light-ion reactions is governed by the statistical decay of a hot composite system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fully and partially energy-damped complex fragments are produced in a similar manner in low-energy light ion reactions.
the deep inelastic fragment emission in low-energy reactions is a fast process, and the dissipation of angular momentum in these reactions is very close to the sticking limit.
the present study of the complex fragment emission is a good example of a complex reaction system where the statistical and the dynamical aspects are well decoupled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deep inelastic emission in low-energy heavy-ion collisions is governed by the sticking limit of the dissipated angular momentum.
the deep inelastic emission in light-ion reactions is governed by the same mechanism as that in heavy-ion collisions, and the sticking limit is a valid concept in this context.
the deep inelastic collisions are the main mechanism for the production of the light complex fragments in low-energy light-ions reactions.
